title: Idols Frankie Trumbauer and Red Nichols
summary: The two recall Trumbauer's C-melody solo on 'Singin' the Blues' and Thomas's admiration for Red Nichols and his Five Pennies.

bands.name: Red Nichols and His Five Pennies

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Well, he said Frankie Trumbauer was his idol, the C-melody saxophone player.
Frankie Trumbauer was half of the saxophone players in the country in that day. Everybody learned how to play that one solo of Frank Trumbauer.
And I'll tell you another idol. Red Nichols.
Red Nichols and his Five Pennies. The way he had them...
Them guys were playing Jazz good enough to record. I don't know... When I came to New York, Red Nichols was playing in a show with Ethel Merman in it, the
one where "I Got Rhythm" came from. And he was... He had the band there. I went down to hear that, because I idolized Red Nichols..
